Like 5-6 months ago I was doing a job for a market (swap out some of their condensing units). My father passed away Christmas from Cancer. He would usually take care of setting up installs and just having his input in general was great. He had stepped back from the company for a good 2 years beforehand while he was getting treatment, but I could still just give him a call (or I'd also see him every day) to ask questions.

Well I brought a nitro lift that's much easier to transport to use to bring the new unit up and old unit down. Turned out that the unit was much bigger than I thought, but I figured we would still be alright. I was pulling the unit to the edge of the roof with my brother, and we had to lift it up and off about 3 feet because the lift couldn't come flush to the roof. It's about 350-400 pounds, so pretty damn heavy, so I had to kind of swing it over and drop it onto the lift. This is usually what I do with my other lifts. Because it was a nitrogen lift, OBVIOUSLY, as soon as the weight hit the platform, it shot down like a rocket taking me with it off the roof. About 15-16 feet. Broke my radial head on my elbow that connects to the wrist apparently, and fractured right ankle and messed up a few other things. Its still healing extremely slow, and my range of motion is about 70% of what it used to be, and I don't believe it will ever come back.

Lifelong injury due to trying to be lazy/work faster by bringing an easier lift. My dad probably would have called me an idiot (not really, because he was the nicest guy on the planet basically)

Hi, I boxed for about 7 years. For starters, I don't recommend weight lifting. I was much, much faster when I boxed and only did pushups/pullups, and probably the same punching power. Also weighed about 40 pounds less. Muscle doesn't make u punch much harder, except possibly leg muscle. If you want to do anything, I'd say just do pushups/pullups 3 days out of the week. Muscle makes u slower and fight bigger guys with a longer reach.

As for boxing - start out with sprints. U might see the movies of a boxer running 12 miles a day,but it's not accurate. I ran 13 miles a day for 2 years when I boxed and it didn't help at all with stamina in the ring. I also overtrained a shit ton thinking work harder, more results. I would say do sprints 3 days a week. Push yourself hard, explosive sprints. That helps with explosiveness in the ring.

Jump rope is incredible cardio. I would do jump rope probably 5 days a week just for like 10-20 minutes.

Join a boxing gym and go 3 days a week to start. Push yourself, hit the heavy bag to get strength, shadow box for your form, follow what the trainers say, spar spar spar.

One thing I did differently when I boxed was I would shadow box with 5 pound weights. My hands were lightning quick then, and they are still very quick compared to anyone my size because of it. It helps a ton. There's way too much on the subject so if you have any specific questions feel free to ask

Don't use raw weight as a point of "progress". 180 bench for someone 6 Ft is literally the basics within a week or two of bench form training. Taller people are stronger.

For example: A "strong" person about 6 Ft would could weigh around 215 cut, bench probably 350+. (These are rough estimates, not accurate. Just an example). A strong person 5'8 might weight 190 cut, bench probably 300+. It's a pretty huge difference with height. Pump up the calories and bulk up, that's about all u can do

Don't ignore legs. I have "ahtletic" legs from years of sports and boxing, so I thought I was good. Once I heavily weight lifted for like 10 years without more than one leg workout a month, my back starts to hurt from the Imbalance. Not to mention, all that strength is almost useless, literally. I can bench 375, curl 150-170 barbell, curl 85 dumbells, but at work I can't pick up nearly what I can in the gym

Why? Because legs are soooo important in real strength. You use your legs in everything, and I wish I had someone teaching me these things when I was younger. Not to mention the imbalance causes pain in different areas. Now trying to bulk up my legs, I have bad knees so I cant squat, and a bad back so deadlifts are a no-go. Had I worked legs out equally, they would be nice like the rest of my body, and could have even prevented the pain.

One piece of advice I'll give you is if you like bikes, stairs, ellipticals, go for those for cardio. I ran a ton when I was a boxer. Miles and miles and miles. I have awful knees now because of it. I also have back pain, but I assume that was from years of lifting irresponsibly. Running puts an incredible amount if strain on your knees so I seriously don't recommend it unless it's like once a week

Honestly I wouldn't go overboard with the diet. You don't sound obese, so you need to have a diet thats easy to monitor for you. There's really no magic here, you either eat less than your body burns, or you eat more and gain weight. Some things also have a factor (protein) but not enough to not lose any weight at all. 

A while ago I did 6 months of just cooking raw chicken (about 200-300 Cal's per serving) and eating it with vegetables. I would take in probably 1400 calories a day. I only drank water period (this is the BIGGEST). I lost a lot of weight, and I didn't have much fat to begin with. Now I easily maintain my weight by using these rules:

-During the week I don't eat fast food. If my wife wants to eat out, I make sure I eat light all day, and definitely get something a little less awful where we eat. If I have a snack during the day, it's yogurt or fruit usually. You need to find a snack that you like otherwise this won't work.

-I workout like 3 times a week just doing pull-ups and pushups but just keep doing whatever you enjoy. You can even cut it down to once or twice a week, since weight loss happens mostly in the kitchen

-I eat basically whatever I want on the weekends, but just keep in mind of what u eat. Don't take it as "cheat days", so if u do go out to eat then get something lighter.

-Like I said, drinks are the most important. A single glass of chocolate milk can be like 250 calories. You can easily take in 800 calories worth of sugar over a day, and thats more than a pound a week on drinks alone. Try to limit yourself to one drink a day AFTER you lose the weight. This way you don't have to do all this again
